arguments.body: Mr Adeyemi, thank you for calling. Safety first: if you can do so safely, switch off the power to your kitchen at the fuse box/consumer unit, and do not touch the light fitting or anything wet near it. Keep clear of the dripping area and move valuables away; put a bucket underneath. If water reaches sockets or you see sparks or smell burning, leave and call 999. We have opened an emergency job and are sending an emergency plumber to Flat 4 to find the source and stop the water. We can't share the tenant's details, but we are trying to contact her and the landlord now. On your ceiling: we can't accept liability or promise payment on this call. Please take photos, keep receipts, and contact your own home insurer; we will pass your details and claim to the landlord, whose buildings insurance may respond. We will update you if we need anything further.

Hi Amelia, urgent: water is coming through the ceiling of the flat below from your flat. We are sending an emergency plumber tonight to get in, find the leak and turn the water off. If you can, please turn off your stopcock (under the kitchen sink) if someone is there, and call us back. We'll update you.

Hi Ben, emergency at Flat 4, 12 Mare Street: the downstairs neighbour (Flat 3) reports water coming through her kitchen ceiling onto a light fitting. Your tenant is away until 12 Oct and not answering. We have instructed Swift Plumbing & Heating to attend tonight, enter using our key if needed (genuine emergency), isolate the water and make safe. We'll tell you the findings and any quote; anything over £300 inc VAT we'll call you first. The neighbour is asking who pays for her ceiling; we have admitted no liability and suggested she contact her insurer. Please notify your buildings insurer. Please call us if you can.

answers.question: Is this an emergency that justifies entering without 24 hours' notice? What conditions apply?
answers.answer: Yes. Active flooding near electrics with the tenant away and unreachable (voicemail, SMS sent). Entry is limited to finding and stopping the leak and making safe, using the office or out-of-hours key with the plumber. Keep a record of the entry and tell the tenant and landlord. Nothing beyond make-safe without the normal notice.

answers.question: What do you tell the caller (who is not your tenant)?
answers.answer: Safety advice (isolate kitchen power at the consumer unit, don't touch the fitting, 999 if sparks), that an emergency plumber is being sent, and that we cannot share the tenant's details but are contacting her. We admit no liability, so no written promise to pay. She should photograph the damage, keep receipts and contact her insurer, and we will pass her claim to the landlord.

answers.question: What actions and notifications do you make, and what must you avoid saying?
answers.answer: Created emergency JOB-101, assigned Swift, messaged the caller, SMS'd the tenant, emailed the landlord and escalated P1. Avoid admitting fault or liability, giving the tenant's number or any personal data, and promising payment or timings not confirmed.

arguments.body: Mr Adeyemi, thank you for calling. Safety first: if you can do so safely, switch off the power to your kitchen at the fuse box/consumer unit, and do not touch the light fitting or anything wet near it. Keep clear of the dripping area and move valuables away; put a bucket underneath. If water reaches sockets or you see sparks or smell burning, leave and call 999. We have opened an emergency job and are sending an emergency plumber to Flat 4 to find the source and stop the water. We can't share the tenant's details, but we are trying to contact her and the landlord now. On your ceiling: we can't accept liability or promise payment on this call. Please take photos, keep receipts, and contact your own home insurer; we will pass your details and claim to the landlord, whose buildings insurance may respond. We will update you if we need anything further.

Hi Amelia, urgent: water is coming through the ceiling of the flat below from your flat. We are sending an emergency plumber tonight to get in, find the leak and turn the water off. If you can, please turn off your stopcock (under the kitchen sink) if someone is there, and call us back. We'll update you.

Hi Ben, emergency at Flat 4, 12 Mare Street: the downstairs neighbour (Flat 3) reports water coming through her kitchen ceiling onto a light fitting. Your tenant is away until 12 Oct and not answering. We have instructed Swift Plumbing & Heating to attend tonight, enter using our key if needed (genuine emergency), isolate the water and make safe. We'll tell you the findings and any quote; anything over £300 inc VAT we'll call you first. The neighbour is asking who pays for her ceiling; we have admitted no liability and suggested she contact her insurer. Please notify your buildings insurer. Please call us if you can.

details.summary: Neighbour in Flat 3 reported water dripping onto a light fitting from Flat 4, whose tenant is away. I opened an emergency job, assigned Swift Plumbing out-of-hours, gave the caller safety advice, refused to share the tenant's number or accept liability, told the tenant and landlord, and escalated P1.

answers.question: Is this an emergency that justifies entering without 24 hours' notice? What conditions apply?
answers.answer: Yes. Active flooding near electrics with the tenant away and unreachable (voicemail, SMS sent). Entry is limited to finding and stopping the leak and making safe, using the office or out-of-hours key with the plumber. Keep a record of the entry and tell the tenant and landlord. Nothing beyond make-safe without the normal notice.

answers.question: What do you tell the caller (who is not your tenant)?
answers.answer: Safety advice (isolate kitchen power at the consumer unit, don't touch the fitting, 999 if sparks), that an emergency plumber is being sent, and that we cannot share the tenant's details but are contacting her. We admit no liability, so no written promise to pay. She should photograph the damage, keep receipts and contact her insurer, and we will pass her claim to the landlord.

answers.question: What actions and notifications do you make, and what must you avoid saying?
answers.answer: Created emergency JOB-101, assigned Swift, messaged the caller, SMS'd the tenant, emailed the landlord and escalated P1. Avoid admitting fault or liability, giving the tenant's number or any personal data, and promising payment or timings not confirmed.
